title: Improve dedicated fleet autoscaler: smoothing token-bucket, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers observed transient tail latency spikes during short bursty traffic (e.g. cron jobs, onboarding spikes). Current token-bucket burst controls allow short bursts but interact poorly with autoscaler smoothing, causing either over-scaling or queueing delays. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) smoother token-bucket adjustments using an exponential moving average to avoid aggressive token replenishment after sustained idle periods, 2) a throughput guarantee signal consumed by the fleet autoscaler that distinguishes short bursts (serve from burst tokens) from sustained demand (scale up), and 3) additional utilization reporting metrics for Dedicated Fleet and the Autoscaler UI to make tuning visible to customers and SREs. Summary of changes: - Autoscaler: new throughput_guarantee signal and logic to delay scaling for bursts under a configurable window (config.dedicated.autoscaler.burst_window_ms) - Token bucket: smoothing factor (token_smoothing_alpha) and a safety cap to prevent immediate full-token refill after idle - Reporting: add dedicated.fleet.utilization.p95_per_queue, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_events, and dedicated.autoscaler.scale_decisions metrics; wire them into telemetry pipeline and Console dashboards - Config & defaults: safe defaults applied for existing Dedicated customers; feature gate autoscaler.smoothing_enabled=false by default for canary rollout - Tests & validation: integration tests for token bucket behavior, unit tests for throughput signal, and end-to-end load test harness updates which reproduce case from SRE-42 Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-1890 - [x] Unit & integration tests added - [x] Load tests + canary rollout plan included - [x] Docs and Console dashboard updates (observability) - [x] Feature gated for staged rollout Rollout plan: enable smoothing in a subset of fleets (10%) for 48h, observe dedicated.autoscaler.scale_decisions and burst_events; if regressions observed rollback by disabling feature gate. If stable, increase to 50% then 100% over two weeks. Impact: Should reduce unnecessary scale-ups during short bursts and reduce tail latency by serving short bursts from tokens while avoiding thrashing of dedicated pools. Related: referenced SUP-321 ticket for customer incident, earlier PRs pr-270111 and pr-302500 for autoscaler policy refactors.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Can you explain why we chose EMA smoothing_alpha=0.25 as default? Seems aggressive for short bursts.
Priya Shah: Chosen after running the replay harness against 3 customer traces; 0.25 balances responsiveness and stability. Added comment and unit tests to validate extremes.
Elena Rodriguez: We need a clear fallback if telemetry pipeline drops the new metrics; prefer using local counters until pipeline confirms delivery.
Priya Shah: Added local counters and a final flush stage so autoscaler falls back to local signals for 5 minutes if ingest errors are observed.
Samir Patel: Please add an integration test that verifies the autoscaler does not scale for bursts shorter than burst_window_ms.
Priya Shah: Added dedicated/tests/autoscaler_burst_window_integration.rs that exercises this path with controlled time advancement.
Marcus Lee: Approved after addressing comments and adding canary rollout script. (LGTM)
merge_commit_summary: autoscaler: smoothing, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting (PR 306789) - adds EMA smoothing for tokenbucket, throughput_guarantee signal, telemetry and dashboard updates, tests, and docs
testing: Unit tests cover tokenbucket smoothing and throughput signal edge cases. Integration test reproduces burst_vs_sustained scenarios with time control. Load harness ran 3 production-like traces from SUP-321 and two internal 1-hour experiments. Canary rollout executed via scripts/canary_rollout.sh at 10% for 48h in staging then promoted to 50% for 72h before full rollout. Observability validated via dedicated.autoscaler.scale_decisions and dedicated.autoscaler.burst_events metrics.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfigured smoothing could delay needed scale-ups for sustained traffic, impacting latency. Mitigation: smoothing disabled by default; staged canary rollout; config override per fleet; autoscaler falls back to sustained throughput signal if burst events exceed threshold; alerting added for scale-decision anomalies. Ops runbook updated in docs/observability/autoscaler.md.
release_notes: Added smoother token-bucket behavior and a throughput guarantee signal to reduce unnecessary scale-ups during short bursts. New metrics and Console dashboard tiles make tuning visible to operators. Feature is feature-gated for staged rollout.
